extracted.intended_audience: general readers and film fans researching the film Superbad
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing the 2007 comedy film Superbad: plot, cast, production, reception, box office, and legacy. Intended as an informational reference about this single film.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes that critics praised the film's dialogue as a positive element contributing to its reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemistry between the two leads
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics praising the chemistry between the two leads
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews highlighted the on-screen chemistry of Jonah Hill and Michael Cera as a key strength of the film.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performances of the supporting cast
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics praising the performances of the supporting cast (Christopher Mintz-Plasse, Seth Rogen, Bill Hader, Martha MacIsaac, Emma Stone, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting performances are singled out as contributing to the film's overall positive reviews and comic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box office / Financial success
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial performance: grossed $170.8 million on a $17.5–20 million budget; opened at #1 with US$33,052,411 opening weekend
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article uses box-office metrics (opening weekend, total domestic and worldwide grosses, comparison to budget) as evidence of commercial success and impact (e.g., 'making it the highest domestic grossing high school comedy at the time').

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical scores / aggregated ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregated critical reception: Rotten Tomatoes approval rating (88%, avg 7.40/10), Metacritic score (76/100), CinemaScore grade (A−)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These numeric/aggregate metrics are presented as measures of critical and audience reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of vulgarity and sincerity (tonal balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Deftly balancing vulgarity and sincerity’ (Rotten Tomatoes summary)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotten Tomatoes' summary frames tonal balance—how the film mixes coarse humor with genuine sentiment—as a criterion for its success and authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of portrayal (friendship / high school experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'authentic take on friendship and the overarching awkwardness of the high school experience' (Rotten Tomatoes summary and other reviews)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers cite authenticity in depicting adolescent friendship and awkwardness as an important qualitative criterion for the film's appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screenplay quality / comedic writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of the screenplay: named among WGA lists (88th greatest of the 21st century; 68th funniest screenplay)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The screenplay's quality and status as a notable comedic script are used as evaluative markers (awards, lists, and industry recognition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and depth compared to similar ensemble comedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical comparisons noting lack of 'smarts or the depths' of comparable ensemble comedies or labeling it 'super-derivative' (e.g., Hollywood Reporter, Orlando Sentinel)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some reviewers evaluate the film on originality and thematic/depthful substance relative to predecessors like American Graffiti or Dazed and Confused; being derivative or lacking depth is a negative criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Listing of awards and nominations (Austin Film Critics, Broadcast Film Critics Association, Chicago Film Critics Association, Empire Awards, MTV Movie Awards, Canadian Comedy Awards, Peabody nomination, Young Hollywood Awards, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards, wins, and nominations serve as formal recognition metrics for artistic and performance quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term cultural legacy / cult status
rubrics_metrics.description: The film 'has since become a cult classic' and is 'considered among the best comedy films of all time' and 'one of the defining films of the Millennial generation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retrospective appraisal, lists, and status (cult classic, placement on best-of lists) are used as measures of enduring cultural significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of origin / autobiographical basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg wrote the script during their teen years; the film is loosely based on their Grade 12 experience and shares the writers' given names for main characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The film's autobiographical roots and the fidelity of adaptation from writers' real-life experience are presented as contextual factors that inform judgments about authenticity and voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controversy / promotional choices (realism vs. legal sensitivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controversy over the special-edition DVD including a replica of the fake McLovin ID that resembled Hawaii's real driver's license leading to its removal from Walmart in Hawaii
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketing/promotional choices and ensuing controversies can affect public reception and are noted as evaluative/impactful events.
